key_insight: One-step generative models do not remove diffusion-like computation; they reorganize denoising across network depth, where intermediate layers can recover the trajectory normally spread across sampling steps.
engineering_relevance: This suggests generative models can be compressed and accelerated by treating depth as an internal time axis, enabling smaller single-pass architectures with similar denoising behavior.
method: Probe intermediate layers using the model’s own output head to decode latent denoising progress.
Compare one-step flow-based models against multi-step diffusion and drifting models.
Train a single time-conditioned block to explicitly model layerwise flow and compress a MeanFlow SiT-L/2 model by 16.6×.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical layer-probing results showing depthwise denoising, including denoise-then-renoise behavior in MeanFlow and successful compression of a MeanFlow SiT-L/2 model by 16.6×.
watch_item: The phenomenon appears to depend on the transport task and model type, so the compression strategy may not transfer to generators without time-indexed transport training.
paper_title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models
